title: Intel NUC 13 Pro mini PC, slim chassis (bought), beside a generated carrier

signals: back: 1 × USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A, 1 × USB 2.0 Type-A, 2 × Thunderbolt 4 Type-C

compute.frame: millimetres, the chassis footprint seen from the top, front panel along the bottom edge, back panel along the top edge, x right, y up

source.where: Intel NUC 13 Pro TPS, section 1.1.4 Table 1 Feature Summary, Max Chassis Dimensions: 'Slim Chassis: 117mm by 112mm x 37mm (including feet)'

also.where: ASUS NUC 13 Pro datasheet, Dimensions (W x D x H): 'K' 117 x 112 x 37 mm

holes.note: no board holes are used: the mini PC mounts by the included VESA bracket, whose hole pattern the TPS doesn't give (measure the bracket)

source.where: Table 2 Additional Features, VESA Mount: 'ship with a VESA mount and screws for attaching the system to compatible screens and monitors'
Table 1, Max Chassis Dimensions: slim chassis 37mm (including feet)
section 2.1.3 Figure 3 Front Panel Connectors and section 2.1.4 Figure 4 Back Panel Connectors; Table 2: Kensington slot 'on the left side of the chassis when viewed from the front'

ports.note: positions along each panel aren't dimensioned

source.where: Table 1, Power Input: '12VDC to 20VDC +/- 5% with DC voltage protection'

inputV.note: ±5% on top of the 12-20 V range; nom is the i5/i7 adapter (20 V), the i3 ships with a 19 V adapter. No USB-C power input is listed: the Thunderbolt ports aren't a supply input

also.where: Power Supply: '20VDC, 6.0A, 120W Power Adapter (i7/i5 CPU)', '19VDC, 4.74A, 90W Power Adapter (i3 CPU)'

peak.note: the supplied adapter's rating (i5/i7), not a measured draw; the i3 adapter is 19 V 4.74 A (90 W). The CPUs are rated cTDP 40 W (i5/i7) and 20 W (i3) in the same datasheet

source.where: Figure 4 Back Panel Connectors: 'A 12-20 V DC Input Jack'

gpioLevel.note: no GPIO header: the link to the MCU board is USB only

source.where: Kit specifications, OS Support: 'Ubuntu 20.04/22.04 LTS 64-bit', 'RedHat Enterprise Linux 9.1 64-bit'

os.note: ASUS lists Ubuntu 22.04, not 24.04: ROS 2 Jazzy (Noble) on this machine isn't vendor-validated

source.where: Humble Hawksbill: amd64 / Ubuntu Jammy (22.04): Tier 1

ros2.note: Jazzy on Ubuntu Noble amd64 is also Tier 1 (REP 2000), but Noble isn't on the vendor's OS list

bridgeDevice.via: the MCU board's native USB (CDC-ACM), one cable per board through the robot's USB-C hub

source.where: Uploading the Application, note: the USB Serial/JTAG Controller's serial port appears 'as /dev/ttyACM* on Linux'

bridgeDevice.note: the first board to enumerate gets ttyACM0; with several MCU boards, pin each by its USB serial number (a udev rule or /dev/serial/by-id) rather than by order. There is no exposed UART on this mini PC, so USB is the only link
